title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are navigating a mix of funding boosts and project setbacks, with the U.S. Space Force securing a hefty budget while grappling with the fallout from canceled NASA projects. Meanwhile, international players like China and Russia are ramping up their launch schedules and co-orbital activities, adding to the complexity of the current landscape.

themes.title: Funding Flows to Space Force
themes.body: The House Appropriations Committee's approval of $55.5 billion for the U.S. Space Force signals a robust commitment to space defense, despite ongoing challenges. This funding boost comes at a time when resilience against threats like GPS jamming is increasingly critical.

themes.title: NASA's Costly Cancellations
themes.body: Canceled NASA exploration projects have left a trail of financial overruns, raising questions about project management and future funding allocations. As the agency recalibrates, the impact on innovation and public trust remains to be seen.

themes.title: International Launch Competition
themes.body: China's upcoming Long March 10B launch reflects its determination to assert itself in the global space race, while Russia's co-orbital maneuvers near commercial GEO slots raise eyebrows. Such activities underscore the geopolitical stakes in space, where every launch is a statement.

themes.title: Emerging Tech Partnerships
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris's collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation bid highlights the growing trend of partnerships in defense tech. As companies jockey for position in the evolving landscape, the emphasis on satellite-control capabilities is becoming increasingly apparent.
